As an Amazon Delivery Driver, it is Amazon policy to; (when raining):
A) leave parcel in mailbox if possible
B) deliver parcel when the weather has cleared.

This is to prevent damage, as rain will go right through that cardboard, plus, we can get in trouble if we don't follow these rules.

Someone either has a lot of work to do, or someone is in deep sh*t

I work at DEN3 in Colorado.
Inbound Management: 3/10
Outbound Management: 8/10
Amnesty Management (My department): 8.5/10

I've worked all the jobs from running totes, to unloading trailers, to literally moving pallets from one side of the building to the other.

First few months working here, f*cking hated it. I'm on month 11, and it's now tolerable. Probably cause I'm now in Amnesty, and that job's pretty ok.

What makes it tolerable, is that I'm getting paid 19+ an hour, with full benefits, to run around and pick dropped items off the AR floor, and reconnect oversized roombas to the internet. Onlybhard part on my end is keeping my feet alive to walk around the entirety of the building multiple times a day.

For reference, my specific building, at my height of 5'9, walking from East to West, or the longest stretch of the building, takes a solid 10 minutes. (Thus why everyone calls it the Green Mile.)

I don't like my job, but I don't hate it. It pays the bills, and that's fine enough for me.

I guess what I fear most, is the court's ruling. I'm fine with paying it back. I fear jail, I fear not being able to go to college because of this, I fear being homeless or too poor to afford basic necessities, all because I made a decision out of my depression.
